title: Fix three write statements
problem: writes.py holds three INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE statements from a chat backend. Each has one bug: one crashes, one would rewrite every message, one removes far more memberships than it should. Fix the SQL so each statement changes exactly the rows it's meant to.
requirements: Keep each statement's parameters in the order given in its comment
ADD_USER inserts username and created_at and lets the database assign the id
EDIT_MESSAGE changes body and edited_at of exactly one message, chosen by id
LEAVE_CHAT removes exactly one (chat, user) membership
A statement that matches no row is not an error: rowcount is 0 and nothing changes
contract: ADD_USER params (username, created_at); EDIT_MESSAGE params (new_body, edited_at, message_id); LEAVE_CHAT params (chat_id, user_id)
expectedBehavior: ADD_USER with ('fay', ...) creates user id 6 (cursor.lastrowid == 6); EDIT_MESSAGE on id 6 has rowcount 1 and leaves the other 15 messages identical; LEAVE_CHAT (1, 2) has rowcount 1
edgeCases: Duplicate username: sqlite3.IntegrityError and no new row
Editing a message id that doesn't exist: rowcount 0, nothing changed
Leaving a chat you're not in: rowcount 0, nothing changed
The user stays in their other chats; the other members stay in this chat
hints: Conceptual: run pytest first and read each failure. Some statements fail with a database error that names the problem; the others run fine but touch the wrong rows. An UPDATE or DELETE touches every row its WHERE allows.

Specific: ADD_USER's VALUES has fewer values than the table has columns. EDIT_MESSAGE has three parameters but only two placeholders. LEAVE_CHAT's condition is true for every row of the chat and every chat of the user.
Implementation: name the columns you insert (INSERT INTO t (col_a, col_b) VALUES (?, ?)); add WHERE id = ? as the last placeholder of the UPDATE; the DELETE needs both conditions to hold at once.
evaluation: The INSERT names its columns instead of relying on the table's column order
Every UPDATE and DELETE has a WHERE that pins down exactly the intended rows
